Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The test `testMissedEndEvent` demonstrates a failure in the DormandPrince853Integrator where the integration proceeds beyond the specified end time (tEvent). The test sets initial time t0 and target tEvent with values that are close but require precise event handling at the end of integration. The failure (integration going past the end time) suggests that the event handling that constrains integration to stop exactly at the end time is not reliable or is being missed due to numerical inaccuracies in event detection.

The integrator under test is DormandPrince853Integrator, which extends AdaptiveStepsizeIntegrator and uses adaptive step sizing and event detection to accurately solve ODEs. The integration step method that performs the solving is `integrate` in AdaptiveStepsizeIntegrator (an abstract method) and implemented in subclasses like DormandPrince853Integrator. Unfortunately, the exact integrate method implementation is not retrieved, but the constructor of DormandPrince853Integrator shows it relies on some static coefficients and a DormandPrince853StepInterpolator for step interpolation.

The current bug report states that the end of integration is handled as an event and numerical accuracy in event detection causes the integrator to overshoot the end time, causing the integration to cover more time than intended. The test shows the overshoot quantitatively, e.g. a 60s range is integrated as about 160s.

The problems likely stem from event detection or event handling logic in the integrator, particularly the logic that detects the final stopping time as an event and truncates integration appropriately. Floating-point precision and step size adaptation could cause this detection to fail or produce imprecise event time location, resulting in integration continuing past the intended stop point.

Recent bug reports are not relevant to this issue as they focus on other algorithms or components.

In summary, the diagnosis is that the failure results from inaccurate or missed detection of the integration end event in the DormandPrince853Integrator due to numerical errors in event location logic when the requested integration range requires precise event timing. This causes the integrator to continue past the specified end of integration.

The focal area for fixing the bug would be the event detection and handling logic in DormandPrince853Integrator (likely in the integrate method and step handling/event location components) to better detect and enforce the integration boundaries.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
